catalog_name: Federated EO Data Space for National Flood Monitoring

providers.sensor_type: Platform (aggregates Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Sentinel-3, Sentinel-5P and additional datasets)
providers.spatial_resolution: Varies by dataset (inherits from hosted missions: 5m - 1km)
providers.revisit_time: Varies by dataset; typically data available within 3-6 hours of satellite acquisition
providers.description: The Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem is the central European platform providing unified access to all Sentinel mission data and derived Copernicus products. It offers a STAC catalogue API, OData API, openEO processing environment, and Jupyter notebook integration. It is the primary access gateway aggregating satellite observations from multiple providers into a single federated discovery and download interface.

flood_detection.notes: Provides unified STAC API access to Sentinel-1 SAR products enabling all-weather flood detection workflows without managing multiple data sources

flood_extent_assessment.notes: Single API endpoint for both Sentinel-1 (all-weather) and Sentinel-2 (optical) data enables combined flood extent workflows

cloudy_conditions.notes: Platform-level access to SAR products enables cloud-independent monitoring; cloud fraction metadata aids observation planning

night_operations.notes: SAR products accessible through CDSE support night-time flood monitoring operations

emergency_response.notes: Fast data access (within hours of acquisition), on-demand processing via openEO, and bulk download capabilities support time-critical emergency operations

strengths: Single STAC API endpoint covering all Sentinel missions and Copernicus products
Free registration with 500 processing units/month included
OData and STAC interfaces for programmatic access
openEO processing environment for cloud-based EO analysis
Jupyter notebook environment with co-located compute
Data available within 3-6 hours of satellite pass
Covers full Sentinel archive from mission start
limitations: Platform access layer, not a primary data source in itself
Free tier has processing unit limits for large-scale cloud processing
STAC catalogue search can be slow for very broad spatiotemporal queries
Requires registration and authentication for data download
products: CCM (Copernicus Contributing Missions) SAR and optical
recommended_for: Unified programmatic access to all Sentinel data for flood monitoring workflows
STAC-based resource discovery across multiple EO collections
Cloud-based processing of large SAR and optical datasets via openEO

providers.sensor_type: Multi-source (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Landsat, MODIS, VHR commercial)
providers.revisit_time: Annual to multi-year updates depending on product; Global Surface Water updated annually
providers.description: The Copernicus Land Monitoring Service delivers pan-European and global land-related datasets including digital elevation models, land cover classification, vegetation, and water-related products. Its datasets provide the essential baseline context for flood risk assessment, hydrological modelling, and post-flood impact analysis.

flood_detection.notes: Not a real-time detection service; provides baseline land and water datasets for context rather than active event monitoring

flood_extent_assessment.notes: Global Surface Water (GSW) product provides 30m long-term water occurrence and change maps enabling flood extent comparison against historical water baselines

cloudy_conditions.notes: Archived products are pre-processed and cloud-free composites; not affected by cloud cover at time of use

night_operations.notes: Static archive products available at any time independent of illumination conditions

emergency_response.notes: EU-DEM provides hydrological terrain analysis; imperviousness layers support urban flood risk; land cover data contextualises flood impact by use type

strengths: EU-DEM v1.1 provides 25m pan-European digital elevation model for hydrological modelling
Global Surface Water (GSW) tracks water body changes from 1984 to present at 30m
CORINE Land Cover classifies land use across Europe for flood impact stratification
High Resolution Layers (HRL): imperviousness, forest, water bodies at 10-100m
Free and open access to all products
Long archive supporting historical baseline analysis
limitations: Not a real-time or near-real-time monitoring system
Products updated annually or less frequently
EU-DEM resolution (25m) insufficient for urban drainage modelling
Primarily European coverage for high-resolution products
products: Global Surface Water (GSW) - occurrence, seasonality, change
High Resolution Layers: imperviousness, forest, grassland, water bodies, small woody features
recommended_for: Baseline flood risk assessment and hydrological modelling
Historical water body change analysis (GSW)
Urban flood impact stratification using imperviousness and land cover
Terrain analysis for flood pathway modelling using EU-DEM

providers.sensor_type: Multi-source (Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2, VHR commercial imagery, UAV)
providers.spatial_resolution: Varies by activation; typically 2.5-10m for rapid mapping products
providers.revisit_time: On-demand activation; rapid mapping products delivered within hours to 1-2 days
providers.description: The Copernicus Emergency Management Service provides on-demand geo-information products for emergency management covering all phases of the disaster management cycle. The Rapid Mapping component delivers flood delineation, grading and damage assessment maps within hours of activation. EFAS and GloFAS provide flood forecasting from 15 to 30 days ahead.

flood_detection.notes: Rapid Mapping delivers standardised flood delineation maps fusing SAR and optical imagery; activation triggered by national civil protection authorities

flood_extent_assessment.notes: Flood extent delineation maps and grading maps (damage severity by land-use class) produced at very high resolution for affected areas

cloudy_conditions.notes: Service integrates all-weather SAR (Sentinel-1) as primary source when clouds prevent optical imaging

night_operations.notes: SAR-based products support night-time operations; service operates 24/7 for emergency activations

emergency_response.notes: Core mission of the service; products directly support civil protection, humanitarian aid and disaster response coordination

strengths: Operationally validated emergency mapping products used by European civil protection agencies
Standardised cartographic output compatible with emergency management workflows
24/7 service availability for activations within Europe and globally
Integrates best available imagery (SAR, optical, VHR) for each event
Includes European Flood Awareness System (EFAS) for 15-day flood forecasting
Global Flood Awareness System (GloFAS) for 30-day global forecasts
Free access to all activation products and historical archive
limitations: Requires formal activation by authorised national civil protection authority
Not a continuous monitoring system; activations are event-driven
Turnaround time for first products typically 12-24 hours after activation
Coverage limited to the declared area of interest
Not suitable for autonomous monitoring without prior activation
products: Flood grading maps (damage assessment by land use)
recommended_for: Activated emergency response requiring validated cartographic products
Multi-day flood event coordination across multiple agencies
Early warning through EFAS/GloFAS forecasting systems

providers.organization: European Organisation for the Exploitation of Meteorological Satellites
providers.sensor_type: SEVIRI (Meteosat MSG geostationary), AVHRR / ASCAT / MHS (Metop polar-orbiting)
providers.revisit_time: 15 minutes (Meteosat MSG SEVIRI); 12-hour repeat (Metop polar orbit)
providers.description: EUMETSAT operates Europe's meteorological satellites providing continuous atmospheric and meteorological monitoring. For flood monitoring, EUMETSAT supplies high-frequency precipitation estimates, soil moisture data, and severe weather products through the Hydrology Satellite Application Facility (H SAF), which are essential for flood early warning and upstream rainfall monitoring.

flood_detection.notes: Meteorological sensors do not detect surface flooding directly; precipitation data supports upstream cause monitoring rather than flood surface detection

flood_extent_assessment.notes: Coarse spatial resolution (3-25km) insufficient for flood extent delineation; atmospheric focus

cloudy_conditions.notes: Microwave precipitation retrievals from Metop (MHS, AMSU) are cloud-penetrating; geostationary SEVIRI IR imagery monitors storm systems regardless of cloud cover

night_operations.notes: IR and microwave instruments operate 24/7 independent of solar illumination; continuous precipitation monitoring day and night

emergency_response.notes: H SAF near-real-time precipitation products feed into EFAS early warning; 15-minute MSG updates enable real-time tracking of extreme rainfall events

strengths: 15-minute precipitation estimates from geostationary Meteosat MSG SEVIRI
Hydrology SAF (H SAF) delivers operational near-real-time precipitation and soil moisture
Continuous 24/7 monitoring over Europe, Africa and the Atlantic
Essential upstream rainfall data for river flood early warning (feeds EFAS)
Long operational record since 1977 enabling climatological flood context
Global coverage via Metop polar-orbiting satellites
limitations: Spatial resolution (3-25km) too coarse for detailed flood extent mapping
Primarily meteorological focus; surface flood detection requires complementary SAR/optical data
Requires user registration and data service agreement for full access
Precipitation retrieval has uncertainty in complex orographic terrain
products: H SAF H60 - instantaneous rain rate (Metop microwave)
H SAF H90 - accumulated precipitation analysis
RGB cloud composites and severe convection products
recommended_for: Upstream rainfall monitoring for river flood early warning
Real-time precipitation tracking during active storm events
Soil saturation assessment before and during flood events
Feeding hydrological models and EFAS with real-time precipitation forcing

providers.revisit_time: 6 days per satellite; ~3 days over Europe with constellation
providers.description: Sentinel-1 is a polar-orbiting, all-weather, day-and-night C-band SAR mission. It is the primary satellite source for flood mapping in Europe and globally, providing backscatter imagery that clearly distinguishes open water from land regardless of cloud cover or lighting conditions.

flood_detection.notes: Open water produces low SAR backscatter in VV/VH polarisation, enabling reliable flood detection through thresholding and change detection

flood_extent_assessment.notes: Pre- and post-event SAR change detection accurately delineates flood extent; IW mode covers 250km swath at 10m resolution

cloudy_conditions.notes: Active SAR sensor penetrates all cloud types, rain and atmospheric aerosols without any signal degradation

night_operations.notes: Active sensor transmits its own microwave pulses, completely independent of solar illumination

emergency_response.notes: Primary data source for Copernicus EMS Rapid Mapping activations; free access within hours of acquisition

strengths: All-weather capability through cloud penetration
Day and night operations with active sensor
10m spatial resolution in Interferometric Wide (IW) mode
250km swath width enabling large area coverage
Free and open access with no registration required for data
Long time series available since April 2014
Constellation restored with Sentinel-1C launch in December 2024
limitations: SAR imagery requires specialist processing skills (speckle, geometric correction)
Flooded vegetation and urban areas produce complex backscatter signatures
Steep or mountainous terrain causes radar shadow and layover artefacts
Reduced repeat cycle from 2021 to 2024 following Sentinel-1B failure
recommended_for: Primary all-weather flood mapping
Rapid mapping during active flood events
Night-time or cloudy emergency response

providers.revisit_time: 5 days at equator; 2-3 days at mid-latitudes (A+B constellation)
providers.description: Sentinel-2 is a polar-orbiting multispectral optical mission optimised for land monitoring. It provides high-resolution surface reflectance imagery enabling accurate computation of spectral water indices (NDWI, MNDWI) for flood extent mapping under clear sky conditions.

flood_detection.notes: NDWI (Green-NIR / Green+NIR) and MNDWI (Green-SWIR / Green+SWIR) indices clearly separate water from land at 10-20m resolution

flood_extent_assessment.notes: Water body delineation from spectral indices provides detailed flood extent maps at 10m resolution in cloud-free conditions

cloudy_conditions.notes: Optical sensor is completely blocked by cloud cover; cloud fraction above 20% severely limits usability during flood events

night_operations.notes: Passive optical sensor requires solar illumination; no night-time acquisition capability

emergency_response.notes: Complementary to SAR for post-event damage assessment in cloud-free windows; 10m resolution supports detailed impact mapping

strengths: 10m spatial resolution in visible and NIR bands
290km swath width for large area coverage
Dedicated water detection bands (B3 Green, B8 NIR, B11/B12 SWIR)
Free and open access with full data continuity since 2015
Rich time series enabling pre-flood baseline computation
Complementary to Sentinel-1 SAR in cloud-free periods
limitations: Completely blocked by cloud cover, which frequently accompanies flood events
No night-time capability
Dense vegetation canopy can mask shallow flooding beneath
Atmospheric correction required for accurate water index computation
recommended_for: Post-event flood extent mapping in clear sky windows
Vegetation and land-use context for flood impact assessment
Multi-temporal analysis comparing pre- and post-flood land cover

providers.sensor_type: OLCI (Ocean and Land Colour Instrument, 21 bands) + SLSTR (Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer)
providers.revisit_time: Less than 2 days globally (A+B tandem constellation)
providers.description: Sentinel-3 is a multi-instrument ocean and land monitoring mission providing global coverage at medium resolution. Its OLCI sensor enables large-scale water body monitoring and flood extent estimation, while SLSTR provides surface temperature data useful for assessing flood-affected areas and evaporation dynamics.

flood_detection.notes: OLCI water bands enable flood detection at 300m resolution; suitable for large river and coastal flood events

flood_extent_assessment.notes: Global Surface Water monitoring at 300m; best suited for large-scale flood extents covering hundreds of square kilometres

cloudy_conditions.notes: Optical instrument; cloud cover limits observations, though near-daily revisit improves cloud-free chance

night_operations.notes: Passive optical sensor; no night-time capability for OLCI

emergency_response.notes: Near-daily coverage supports operational monitoring of evolving large-scale flood situations

strengths: Near-daily global revisit (< 2 days with A+B tandem)
Wide area coverage at 300m enabling continental-scale flood monitoring
21 OLCI spectral bands optimised for water and land colour
Synergy between OLCI and SLSTR instruments
Free and open access
Consistent long-term record since 2016 (3A) and 2018 (3B)
limitations: 300m resolution too coarse for detailed urban or small river flood mapping
Optical instrument blocked by clouds
Less commonly used than Sentinel-1/2 for emergency flood response
recommended_for: Large-scale river basin and coastal flood monitoring
Continental overview of flood evolution over multiple days
Land surface temperature change detection in flooded areas

providers.description: Sentinel-5P carries the TROPOMI instrument for daily global atmospheric monitoring at unprecedented spatial resolution. While primarily an atmospheric mission, it supports flood emergency response by detecting methane releases from flooded wetlands, monitoring NO2 and SO2 from industrial accidents accompanying floods, and assessing aerosol and cloud coverage to plan optical satellite observations.

flood_detection.notes: Atmospheric sensor; does not directly detect surface flooding

flood_extent_assessment.notes: 3.5km resolution and atmospheric focus make it unsuitable for flood extent delineation

cloudy_conditions.notes: Cloud fraction and aerosol products identify when and where optical satellite observation windows are available

night_operations.notes: Passive UV/VIS instrument requires solar illumination for most products

emergency_response.notes: Detects methane (CH4) from flooded organic soils and wetlands; monitors NO2/SO2 from industrial accidents triggered by flooding; supports multi-hazard emergency assessment

strengths: Daily global atmospheric coverage
Highest-resolution spaceborne atmospheric spectrometer for operational use
Detects secondary hazards co-occurring with floods (industrial accidents, gas leaks)
Cloud fraction product guides planning of optical satellite tasking
Free and open access
Available since October 2017
limitations: Does not detect surface flooding directly
3.5km pixel size far too coarse for flood extent mapping
Primarily an atmospheric instrument; flood applications are ancillary
Requires atmospheric chemistry expertise to interpret correctly
recommended_for: Multi-hazard emergency assessment alongside surface flood mapping
Methane monitoring from flooded organic soils
Optical satellite observation window planning using cloud fraction data
